items.title: Branford Marsalis — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Well, what’s Muammar Gaddafi, if Wynton is controversial?

ctx.x: Sound like a bunch of kids. Bunch of kids who were playing jazz, and allowed to play jazz because of the vacuum that I told you about earlier, where there just weren’t a bunch of guys playing it. So, we were able to kind of sneak in there. But if we were playing the way we played, and we tried to do that in 1960… nothing. “Keep trying kids.” But then we would have had to have practiced more. The whole thing would have been different. There was just this big vacuum there for that style of music. Trying to play…

I’m buying suits. (laughs about this with AB) Because I just didn’t…because of the way my father grew up, we didn’t grow up…My father and my mother, well mostly my father, was not… did not really care about how he was perceived by other people.
